description: Shared correctness fixtures (docs/benchmark-correctness-fixtures.md). One shared pool of six deterministic integer strategies (s0..s5) is dispatched over three named input domains (pricingFunctions: linear i; codecStrategies: xorshift64 stream seed=42; validationRules: xorshift64 stream seed=43) — the variable under test is CALL-SITE SHAPE (how many distinct concrete implementations a call site sees), not per-domain business logic, so the strategy pool is deliberately shared across datasets (documented in java.md/rust.md). Two pairwise equalities are the correctness oracle: monomorphic == oversizedCallee (same single strategy, different code size), and megamorphic == switchDispatch (same six-way round-robin, different dispatch mechanism). bimorphic has its own total (a genuinely different assignment pattern, no manual-dispatch counterpart in this lab).

semantics.strategies: s0(x)=x+1; s1(x)=x*3; s2(x)=x^0x5A5A; s3(x)=(x<<1)+7; s4(x)=x-11; s5(x)=(x>>2)|1 — six DISTINCT concrete implementations of one shared interface/trait
semantics.xorshift64: x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 7 (unsigned/logical); x ^= x << 17 (64-bit wrapping, unsigned interpretation throughout)
semantics.pricingFunctions: input[i] = i for i in [0, n) — linear, no RNG
semantics.monomorphicAssignment: strategy index = 0 for every i (a single concrete type at the call site)
semantics.bimorphicAssignment: strategy index = i mod 2 (exactly two concrete types at the call site)
semantics.megamorphicAssignment: strategy index = i mod 6 (all six concrete types at the call site, round-robin)
semantics.switchDispatchAssignment: IDENTICAL to megamorphicAssignment (i mod 6) but dispatched via a closed switch/enum match instead of interface/trait-object polymorphism
semantics.oversizedCalleeAssignment: IDENTICAL to monomorphicAssignment (always strategy 0) but implemented as a deliberately bloated method body computing the same result
